name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Ghostwriter is a Java command-line documentation and AI workflow engine from Machanism MachAI. It scans project trees, detects embedded @guidance directives in source and documentation files, builds project-aware prompts, and dispatches those prompts to configured GenAI providers. The artifact provides processors for guidance-driven review, reusable TOML-defined Acts, multi-episode workflow control, project context variables, host-integrated file tools, command execution tools with deny-list security, web and REST access tools, bounded command log handling, and reviewer implementations for Java, Markdown, HTML/XML, PlantUML, Python, TypeScript, and @guidance.txt files. It is useful for AI-assisted documentation generation, project analysis, automated code review workflows, act-based developer automation, and Maven/Java project documentation pipelines.

examples.title: Install Ghostwriter as a Maven dependency
examples.scenario: Use Ghostwriter classes inside a Java application or tool.
steps: Add the Maven dependency org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter:1.2.2-SNAPSHOT to your pom.xml.
Ensure the MachAI snapshot repository is configured if the version is not available in Maven Central releases.
Instantiate org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.GuidanceProcessor or org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.ActProcessor with a project directory, model identifier, and configurator.
examples.snippet:
<repositories>
  <repository>
    <id>central-snapshots</id>
    <url>https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots</url>
    <snapshots><enabled>true</enabled></snapshots>
    <releases><enabled>false</enabled></releases>
  </repository>
</repositories>
<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.machanism.machai</groupId>
    <artifactId>ghostwriter</artifactId>
    <version>1.2.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
examples.description: This configuration installs the Ghostwriter library into a Maven project so applications can use its processors, reviewers, and tools programmatically.

examples.title: Run Ghostwriter as a CLI component
examples.scenario: Build and invoke the command-line documentation engine for a real project.
steps: Build the assembled CLI jar with Maven using the pack profile.
Configure a GenAI model and Act location through project configuration or runtime properties.
Run the Ghostwriter main class and choose a scan path or act workflow according to your host configuration.
examples.snippet:
mvn -Ppack install
java -cp target/gw.jar org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter --help
examples.description: The pack profile assembles a runnable Ghostwriter jar whose main class is org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter. The help output shows available command-line options for scanning and AI workflow execution.

examples.title: Process @guidance tags in source files
examples.scenario: Ask Ghostwriter to inspect source files containing embedded guidance comments and generate AI-assisted improvements or documentation.
steps: Add @guidance comments to Java, Markdown, HTML/XML, Python, TypeScript, PlantUML, or @guidance.txt files.
Create a GuidanceProcessor with the current project directory and model identifier.
Call scanDocuments with a directory, glob pattern, or regex pattern to select files.
examples.description: This example scans all Java source files for @guidance comments, sends extracted instructions to the configured model, and obtains a processing report.

examples.title: Run an Act against generated Javadoc
examples.scenario: Use the built-in mvn/extract-javadoc Act to extract structured information from Javadoc HTML files.
steps: Generate Javadoc or Maven site output so target/reports/apidocs contains HTML files.
Create an ActProcessor with the current project and model.
Scan target/reports/apidocs using a recursive glob.
examples.description: This practical workflow extracts API metadata from generated Javadoc and can be used as input for bindex.json generation.

examples.title: Use host-integrated function tools in an AI workflow
examples.scenario: Expose safe project operations such as reading files, executing commands, fetching web content, and storing context to an AI provider.
steps: Instantiate the tool class needed by the workflow, such as FileFunctionTools, CommandFunctionTools, WebFunctionTools, ActFunctionTools, or ProjectContextFunctionTools.
Pass project-relative paths and a host-controlled project directory.
Use command execution only when allowed by host policy and deny-list checks.
examples.description: This example reads a project file and stores workflow context for later act episodes or AI tool calls.
